name: Cashew nut oil lightening
lead: Cashew nut oil lightening is a folk practice in which people apply cashew-derived oil to the skin hoping to lighten it or even tone. It is reported in folk-remedy circles to burn skin.

The oil in question is usually cashew nutshell liquid, the resin from the shell. Its main components, anacardic acids, cardol and cardanol, are strong skin irritants related to the allergens in poison ivy [1].

chain: Intended: lighter or more even tone
angle.text: People try it hoping for a lighter, more even complexion. The oil is an irritant, which is the main reported outcome.

paras: Cashew nutshell liquid is a yellowish resin in the shell's honeycomb structure and a byproduct of cashew processing. It is described as a strong irritant and is dangerous to handle [1]. It has traditional uses in folk medicine [1].
Shell oil compounds can cause contact dermatitis similar to poison ivy, which is why cashews are generally not sold in the shell [1].

card.summary: A folk practice of applying cashew-derived oil to skin hoping to lighten tone; the oil is a known irritant.
card.note: Cashew shell oil can burn skin and cause contact dermatitis.

quick.overview:
Some people apply cashew-derived oil to skin to try to lighten it.

The oil from the shell is a strong irritant.
quick.mechanism: Its phenolic compounds irritate the skin; no study shows a lightening mechanism.
quick.risks: Burns and contact dermatitis resembling poison ivy are reported.
